studies.objective: Compare captures and checks before accepting a rook offer.

studies.title: King activity before counting pawns
studies.objective: Consider how the king can support the advanced kingside pawn.
studies.explanation: Kg3 moves the king from f3 toward h4, g5 and f6 in the actual continuation. Black can take c3 with check, so White must calculate king safety rather than simply compare pawn counts. Replay how the king and g-pawn coordinate; this study does not claim that every material sacrifice wins.

studies.title: Calculate before saving the queen
studies.objective: Compare moving the threatened queen with a forcing counterattack.
studies.explanation: Black plays Be6 while the queen on b6 is attacked by White’s bishop on c5. After the historical Bxb6, Bxc4+ checks the king and the knight joins a sequence of forcing moves. Calculate those legal replies before judging the queen offer. A historical choice is a comparison exercise, not an assertion of a unique forced solution.
